title: Attainable linear complexities of de Bruijn sequences
summary: Characterize exactly which values in the known interval occur as linear complexities of binary de Bruijn sequences.

formal_statement.body: For every admissible order $n\ge 3$, define $S_n=\{LC(s):s\text{ is a binary de Bruijn sequence of order }n\}$. Determine $S_n$ exactly. In particular, decide for every integer $L$ satisfying $2^{n-1}+n\le L\le 2^n-1$ whether there is an order-$n$ de Bruijn sequence $s$ with $LC(s)=L$.

scope.domain: Binary de Bruijn sequences and linear complexity
assumptions: A sequence of order n is binary, periodic with period 2^n, and contains every n-bit word exactly once per period
LC(s) denotes the linear complexity of the periodic sequence s
scope.unresolved_remainder: No exact characterization of the attainable set is known over the full order range; search algorithms and partial-cycle constructions do not determine the linear-complexity spectrum.

provenance.note: The 2022 TIT paper cites Chan--Games--Key for the known interval, but the exact earliest statement of the attainability problem was not text-confirmed.

citations.label: Li--Lin, adjacency graphs of affine FSRs

progress.summary: The source gives the known numerical interval and explicitly states that the attainable values within it remain unknown.
